metadata.title: IEA International Computer and Information Literacy Study 2023 Assessment Framework
metadata.venue: IEA International Computer and Information Literacy Study 2023

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This publication is an assessment framework for ICILS 2023 rather than an empirical analysis paper. It specifies the target population (students in the eighth year of schooling, or grade 9 where grade 8 average age is below 13.5) and the sampling approach (schools selected with PPS and one intact class selected within each school), along with parallel sampling logic for teachers and school ICT coordinators. Because no analysis results are reported here, the framework does not document which student/sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were applied in estimation. For users of ICILS microdata, weighting and replicate design should follow the ICILS data user documentation; this framework focuses on constructs, instruments, and test design rather than estimation implementation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a framework/documentation volume describing the ICILS 2023 assessment design, constructs, and instruments, not a study that estimates predictive models or reports achievement outcomes from student-level data. As such, there is no analysis section specifying how plausible values (PV-based achievement scores) or missing data were handled. The absence of PV and missing-data handling details is therefore by design: the document is intended to guide assessment implementation and interpretation rather than to provide an empirical estimation pipeline.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Target student population: students in their eighth year of schooling (typically grade 8; if average age in grade 8 is below 13.5 years, the adjacent upper grade 9 is used). Schools are selected randomly proportional to size (PPS), and within each sampled school one intact class of the target grade is selected randomly. Teacher survey target: all teachers teaching regular subjects at the target grade; within each school, 15 eligible teachers are randomly selected if more than 20 eligible teachers exist, otherwise all eligible teachers are selected. School-level data are collected from the principal and ICT coordinator of each sampled school; national contexts are provided by ICILS national research centers.

data.outcome_summary: This ICILS 2023 Assessment Framework publication documents how the International Computer and Information Literacy Study operationalizes its core learning outcomes—Computer and Information Literacy (CIL) and Computational Thinking (CT)—and how these are measured through authentic computer-based tasks administered to students in their eighth year of schooling. It specifies the study’s target population and sampling logic (PPS school selection and one intact class per school), and it describes the suite of instruments: student questionnaire, teacher questionnaire, principal questionnaire, ICT coordinator questionnaire, and a national contexts survey. The framework also explains how CIL and CT constructs are structured and how test modules are organized around real-world scenarios, including the evolution of CT modules in 2023. Because this is a design framework rather than an empirical results paper, it does not report model performance metrics, benchmarks, or statistical effects. Policy relevance lies in ensuring that subsequent ICILS analyses can interpret CIL/CT scores consistently across cycles and countries, supporting valid comparisons and informed digital-skills policy decisions.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is an assessment framework (methodology/design documentation) rather than an empirical study estimating relationships between predictors and ICILS outcomes. Consequently, there is no analytic sample size, no country-level sample breakdown, no PV/missing-data estimation strategy, and no ML model training or predictive performance reported. The extraction therefore leaves empirical ML fields empty and focuses on the documented sampling and instrument design needed for later analyses using ICILS 2023 microdata.
